How attackers infiltrated secure banking infrastructure
How fraudulent SWIFT messages were crafted and executed
The critical error that stopped a $1 billion theft

Companies were paying double and triple on the secondary market just to get them faster.In 2023 alone Nvidia's stock went up 239%.

snippet.description:

In 1984, the greatest athlete of all time wanted Adidas. He had no interest in Nike. His mother, Deloris Jordan, was the one who insisted he at least show up to the meeting. He went. He sat through the pitch. He was unimpressed.

Then in 2010 he bought the Charlotte Hornets NBA team for $275 million. In 2023 he sold his majority stake for $3 billion — the largest sale of a major North American sports team at that time.

His total net worth today: $3.5 billion. Not from basketball. From a contract. From a royalty. From a meeting his mother told him to attend.

The greatest athlete of the 20th century became a billionaire not on the court — but in the boardroom. And it all happened because one woman said go to that meeting.

snippet.title: Every Time You Tap Your Card, Two Companies Silently Take Your Money — And Nobody Talks About It 💳💰
snippet.description:
Every single time you tap your card anywhere in the world — at a restaurant, a grocery store, a gas station, online, anywhere — two companies take a cut.

They don't lend you money.

They don't hold your deposits.

They don't take any risk whatsoever.

They just sit invisibly in the middle of every transaction on Earth.

And they collect a fee every single time.

Meet Visa and Mastercard.

The most quietly dominant duopoly in the history of finance.

Here's how it works.

When you tap your card, your bank talks to the store's bank. But they don't talk directly — they talk through Visa or Mastercard's network. And for providing that connection, Visa and Mastercard charge a fraction of a percent on every single transaction.

Fractions of a percent sounds like nothing.

Multiplied across hundreds of billions of transactions every year — it's everything.

Visa processes 212 billion transactions annually.

Mastercard processes 120 billion.

Together they control 90% of all card transactions outside China.

Mastercard went public in 2006.

Its stock has risen over 20,000% since then.

Visa went public in 2008.

Up over 1,500% since then.

Both companies consistently post profit margins above 50%.

For context — Apple's profit margin is around 25%.

Visa and Mastercard make twice the profit per dollar of revenue as one of the most valuable companies ever built.

And here's the most beautiful part of the business model.

Every time a new country modernizes its financial system — they join the Visa and Mastercard network.

Every time cash payments go digital — Visa and Mastercard get richer.

Every time a new online marketplace launches — Visa and Mastercard clip the ticket.

They don't need to innovate.

They don't need to take risks.

They just need the world to keep buying things.

And the world always keeps buying things.

Visa and Mastercard built the greatest toll road in human history.

There is no asphalt.

There are no workers.

There is no physical infrastructure.

A young billionaire, Elizabeth Holmes, claimed her company could run hundreds of medical tests using just a few drops of blood.

Investors poured in billions. The media crowned her the “next Steve Jobs.” And some of the most powerful people in the world believed her vision.

The company was called Theranos.

But behind the headlines, the technology didn’t work… and the truth was far more shocking than anyone imagined.

Within just a few years, Theranos would be exposed as one of the biggest frauds in modern tech history—shattering trust, destroying reputations, and changing Silicon Valley forever.
